name: Tooltip
description: Short hint on hover or keyboard focus. Works with CSS alone; with React Tooltip or <ayy-tooltip> it moves to the top layer (never clipped) and flips at screen edges.

classes.ayy-tooltip: Wrapper around the trigger. Shows the content on :hover and :focus-within.
classes.ayy-tooltip__content: The bubble (role="tooltip"). Placement via data-side="top|bottom|start|end" (start/end follow text direction).

default.looks: Hidden. The bubble is a raised surface with a line-strong border and 2xs text.

hover.looks: The bubble fades and slides in after 200ms.

pressed.none: No pressed look; the trigger keeps its own.

focus.looks: The bubble shows at once (no delay) while the trigger has focus.

disabled.none: A disabled button gets no focus and shows no tooltip; explain why it's disabled in visible text instead.

error.none: Never put errors in a tooltip; use a FieldError.

dismissed.looks: Stays hidden until the pointer and focus leave.

sizes.width: As wide as its text, at most 16rem, then wraps.

js: tooltipClass, tooltipContentClass constants; enhanceTooltip(host) moves the bubble to the top layer and adds Esc (returns cleanup).

element.children: One focusable trigger and a .ayy-tooltip__content bubble. Ids and aria-describedby are wired for you.

props.children: One focusable element; aria-describedby is added for you

a11y: Trigger must be focusable so keyboard users see it too.
aria-describedby links trigger → tooltip (React does it automatically).
Esc dismisses (WCAG 1.4.13); the bubble stays open while hovered.
do: Use a tooltip to name icon-only buttons visually (they still need aria-label) and for short clarifications: shortcuts, truncated values.
Use side="start"/"end", not left/right, so RTL works.
Inside overflow:hidden containers, use the React component or <ayy-tooltip> — the CSS-only version can be clipped there.
dont: Don't put essential information in a tooltip — tooltips are invisible on touch devices.
Don't put interactive content (links, buttons) in a tooltip — use a popover or dialog.
Don't wrap disabled buttons — they can't receive focus or hover events reliably.
